subject: URGENT: CloudKart checkout surge — suspected proxy/DNS path issues
messages:
From: Natalie Li <ops@cloudkart.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: High error rate + 95th%-tile latency spike since 09:05 PST

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and 95th%-tile tail latency on checkout calls to Redwood since ~09:05 PST. Impact: ~30% of checkout attempts are returning errors (502/504) or taking 4–12s; downstream orders are timing out and customer drop rate has increased.

What we've gathered so far:
- Errors originate from requests routed to nodes in your us-west cluster (see logs attached).
- Client-side DNS lookups for a subset of Redwood endpoints intermittently time out before retrying.
- Traces show a burst of TCP retransmits and increased RTTs around 09:04–09:08.

We've attached client_logs.tar.gz with sample traces and the checkout request IDs. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your egress/peering side? This is affecting our marketing flash sale—need urgency.

Thanks,
Natalie Li
Director, Site Reliability — CloudKart
ops@cloudkart.com
[attachment: client_logs.tar.gz (gzip)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Li <ops@cloudkart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + 95th%-tile latency spike since 09:05 PST

Hi Natalie — thank you for the quick heads up and for the logs. We're on this.

Immediate plan:
- Rafael and our incident SREs are triaging traces now (cc'd).
- I'll open a dedicated incident bridge at 09:30 PST and loop in netops.
- We will share a short mitigation ETA within 30 minutes and a customer-facing update within 60 minutes.

Can you confirm if you saw the issue across multiple regions or only affecting traffic routed through our us-west egress? Also sending any packet captures you can is helpful.

We take this seriously — apologies for the disruption, we'll escalate as needed.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: RE: High error rate + 95th%-tile latency spike since 09:05 PST

Quick triage notes (prelim):
- I've pulled the client logs and a sample pcap from CloudKart (attached). Initial correlation: a set of ECMP paths from our us-west peering fabric shows transient BGP flap/AS-path changes starting 09:03:51 that coincide with DNS timeouts and SYN retransmits.
- DNS: Lookups for api.redwood.ai show 2–3s timeouts intermittently; caching on client retries masks some failures but not for all flows.
- TCP: Increased RTOs and duplicated ACKs between 09:04–09:09; RTTs jumped from ~18ms to ~320ms for affected paths.

Attachments: tcptrace.txt, vpc_peering_trace.csv (BGP next-hop changes and timestamps).
Suggested immediate mitigations:
1) Fail traffic for CloudKart to fallback region us-west-2 (route override) to minimize impact — cutover in 10 minutes if approved.
2) Reduce cache TTL on gateway DNS to 30s and enable prefix-based routing to avoid the suspect peer.
3) Rate-limit retries on proxy layer to avoid amplification during client-side retry storms.

I'll keep digging; if this is a peering provider-level flap we should get them on the line. Recommend exec attention if SLA hit looks material.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: tcptrace.txt (text)]
[attachment: vpc_peering_trace.csv (csv)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: ACTION REQUIRED: CloudKart checkout surge — request for exec sync

Marissa / Jonas — short summary:
- Customer: CloudKart — high error-rate and multi-second tail latency on checkout since 09:05 PST.
- Impact: Checkout failures for ~30% of requests; flash-sale revenue at risk.
- Probable cause: transient peering/BGP path churn impacting DNS+TCP for a subset of egress routes (see Rafael's traces).

Planned actions (now):
A) Immediate: route override for CloudKart traffic to us-west-2 and enable DNS short-circuiting (10–15 minute execution window).
B) Short-term: tighten proxy retry logic to reduce retry amplification; pause any non-essential background batch jobs for affected customers.
C) Long-term: work with provider to get BGP flap root-cause, and add additional fallback peers + health-check-driven route steering.

We should call CTO/Head of Ops for awareness (possible SLA credit if downtime > 30m). Request your authorization to proceed with A/B above and to draft an exec-facing brief (attaching SLA impact snapshot).

— Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

— Marissa Cole

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Li <ops@cloudkart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Update: mitigation complete — CloudKart checkout traffic routed to fallback region

Hi Natalie — quick update and next steps.

Summary:
- At ~10:10 PST we performed a controlled route override for CloudKart traffic to our us-west-2 cluster and lowered DNS gateway TTLs. We also applied a temporary proxy retry limit to reduce amplification.
- Customer-observed result: error rate dropped from ~30% to <1% within 6 minutes of cutover; 95th%-tile latency returned to expected ranges.

What we did/why:
- Rafael's traces indicated intermittent BGP/peering churn that was causing DNS and TCP path instability for a subset of egress routes. The route override steered traffic away from the impacted peer and stabilized RTTs.

Next steps:
- We're engaging the peering provider and AcornCloud NetOps to get a root-cause and timeline for a permanent fix.
- We'll produce a full RCA and customer-impact summary within 48 hours and share proposed SLA remediation if applicable.

Thanks for your patience — we'll follow up with the RCA and a post-incident call if you'd like to review traces together.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
